key_insight: The paper builds a non-intrusive reduced-order model for chaotic flows by adapting radial basis functions to local attractor geometry, enabling a smooth vector field that reproduces long-term statistics without using the governing equations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate modeling strategy for turbulent and chaotic systems when accurate invariant measures and statistics matter more than pointwise trajectory prediction.
method: Cluster the reduced-state data to identify regions with different local manifold geometry.
Shape a radial basis function library with region-specific kernels, then fit one global regularized least-squares model.
Use a kinematic corrector only to stabilize trajectories that drift off the learned field, and track its magnitude as a trust indicator.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, and Kolmogorov flow, reproducing attractors, densities, Lyapunov exponents, energy spectra, and invariant measures, with competitive forecast horizons against neural-network and reservoir-computing baselines.
watch_item: Because the learned radial basis field decays away from the training data, stability relies on the added corrector, so extrapolation far from the data manifold may be less trustworthy.
paper_title: Manifold-adapted radial basis functions for reduced-order modelling of chaotic flows
